summary: Specifies the Echo service, which sends back to the sender any data it receives. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

plainLanguage.summary: You say something and the computer says it right back, like a parrot.

what is the udp echo service
subtitle: A tiny service that sends back whatever it receives, used as a debugging and measurement tool.

tldr.problem: Operators need a very simple way to debug and measure a network path.
tldr.mechanism: An echo service sends back to the originating source any data it receives, on port 7 over either TCP or UDP.
tldr.outcome: Hosts that choose to implement an Echo Protocol are expected to follow this standard.

today: RFC 862 is an Internet Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What an Echo Service Is
sections.content: The RFC calls an echo service a very useful debugging and measurement tool. It simply sends back to the originating source any data it receives. Hosts that choose to implement an Echo Protocol are expected to adopt this standard; implementing it is optional.
sections.plainLanguage: Send it anything and it hands the same thing back, which shows the connection works.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Echo
sections.content:
The TCP-based service is connection based. A server listens for TCP connections on port 7. Once a connection is established, any data received is sent back, and this continues until the calling user terminates the connection.

The UDP-based service is datagram based. A server listens for UDP datagrams on port 7. When a datagram is received, its data is sent back in an answering datagram.
sections.plainLanguage: On a phone call (TCP) it repeats everything until you hang up. By postcard (UDP) it mails back each postcard's message.

sections.title: Standard Status
sections.content: RFC 862 is an Internet Standard from May 1983. The text is short and defines only the two port 7 behaviors above; it sets no message format, limits or security rules.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a very small rulebook with only two rules: listen on number 7 and send back what you hear.
